title: Late deliveries by region and carrier
prompt: Operations reviews late deliveries by the sending warehouse's region and the shipment's carrier. Write `solve(deliveries, shipments, warehouses)` so it returns `region`, `carrier`, `late_deliveries` and `late_units`.
rules: Count only deliveries whose `status` is `late`. `late_units` is the total `quantity` of their shipments.
A late delivery whose shipment isn't in `shipments` is left out. One whose warehouse isn't in `warehouses` counts in a group with `region` missing.
One row per region and carrier that has late deliveries. Return only these four columns, in this order.
hints: Filter the late deliveries first, then join `shipments` on `shipment_id` to get the carrier, quantity and warehouse.
Which join type drops deliveries with no shipment? Which keeps shipments whose warehouse isn't listed? `warehouses` is the small side to broadcast.
Group by both columns and use `F.count("*")` and `F.sum("quantity")` in one `agg`.
explanation: Filter first so the joins only carry late deliveries. An inner join with `shipments` drops deliveries whose shipment is unknown, because there's no carrier to report. A left join with `F.broadcast(warehouses)` keeps every late shipment and leaves `region` missing when its warehouse isn't listed, and `groupBy("region", "carrier")` then puts those in a group of their own. The broadcast only spares the big side a shuffle: a sort-merge join for the same query returns the same groups, so the grading checks the rows. Counting `status != "on_time"` would also count failed deliveries, which aren't late.
